facts.text: I am trying to work on a project that I started at a Python workshop I attended last month.
I am having issues with my code and I want help debugging it.
I am working on a simple game using Python.
I started the game project at a 3-day workshop on Python programming I attended at the beginning of last month.
The Python workshop was organized by the coding community at the local university.
The project is a team effort.
The team is trying to implement a scoring system but is having trouble with the logic.
We are building a simple 2D platformer game.
In the game, the player collects coins to increase their score.
The score should increase by 10 points for each coin collected.
Right now, the score is not updating correctly.
We tried using a global variable to store the score, but it is not working as expected.
Our team leader is Rachel.
Rachel suggested using a class to encapsulate the game state, including the score.
We have not tried using that class approach yet.
I am thinking about implementing a more flexible scoring system.
I am considering different types of coins worth different points.
I am thinking about implementing a power-up system that gives players temporary advantages.
The power-up system should include increased speed or invincibility.
I want to integrate the power-up system into the game state class.
I want the best way to handle the power-up's duration and effects.
